### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **46** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**36** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 896bfc4762e695f57371f867d15fbb82edbb7ee0`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 896bfc4762e695f57371f867d15fbb82edbb7ee0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d3abd8ba8a9c093102416e69d3048a65b8e255d1` — the merge of head `c018389cb10add586b3555ad5cd7ed56e7c7b1eb` into base `896bfc4762e695f57371f867d15fbb82edbb7ee0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d3abd8ba8a9c093102416e69d3048a65b8e255d1 && git checkout d3abd8ba8a9c093102416e69d3048a65b8e255d1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 896bfc4762e695f57371f867d15fbb82edbb7ee0 c018389cb10add586b3555ad5cd7ed56e7c7b1eb && git checkout -B drift-repro 896bfc4762e695f57371f867d15fbb82edbb7ee0 && git merge --no-ff c018389cb10add586b3555ad5cd7ed56e7c7b1eb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 896bfc4762e695f57371f867d15fbb82edbb7ee0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 896bfc4762e695f57371f867d15fbb82edbb7ee0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8b2d85102b37860101ab9b4598b9d2897e34550f`
Local-runs: probe — a scratch worktree at the head, removed afterwards: the PR's #37013 cases, twelve ablations and thirteen probe cases under `packages/metadata`, and `packages/spec/src/ai/skill.test.ts`, run with vitest to measure which changed paths a test pins and what the unchanged readers answer
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-protection.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts + packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/memory-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/loader-interface.ts, packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.test.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/skill.test.ts
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

First review of PR #37021 (card #37013), a full L1 + L2 read at head `8b2d8510`, base `a73edb3cd`. The PR is 56 files, +591 −104: eight source files, three test files, one changeset and 44 regenerated reference pages. `main` has moved five commits to `8e4ac50d4` (80 files, none of them the PR's). The PR is a draft and auto-merge is not armed. Inputs: the diff, the card and its two comments (the claim and the os-dev-report), the PR body, AGENTS.md, ADR-0150 and ADR-0010, and the check-runs at the head. Code read to judge the diff, not reviewed: `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts` and `protocol-package-bindings.ts`, `packages/spec/src/shared/protection.zod.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts`, `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts`. Line numbers are at this head.

The write and removal rules the card asks for are in the store and hold where the PR tests them: with the registry holding both records, the platform's record and a package's item of the name keep a slot and a row each, and the platform's write and withdrawal leave the package's alone. The verdict is FAIL on three must-fix findings. Each finding has a grade.

- **R1 (must-fix):** three checks are red at this head, all on the hand-written type mirror the PR leaves for later.
- **R2 (must-fix):** the rule "no other write carries the stamp" holds at `register` and at no other seam.
- **R3 (must-fix):** the read and enumerate seams still read the platform's record by the rule for a package-less item, so "both readable" and "`list` returns both" hold from a warm registry and not from the stored rows.
- **R4 (should-fix):** for a bundled type the loader's row predicate reads the slot's first row, not the row the write takes over.
- **R5 (should-fix):** four changed paths have no failing pin.
- **R6 (should-fix, the maintainer's to land):** ADR-0150 D4 and ADR-0010 §3.5 state rules this PR changes and carry no amendment note.
- **R7 (the seat's, no code asked):** card item 3 and the code differ for an environment write that names no package. It is a deviation from the item as written, and not from the Acceptance line.
- **R8 (should-fix):** for a type outside the by-package set the withdrawal takes the name's item whoever wrote it.
- **R9 (nit):** three texts trail the change.

### ① Derived judgments

**Card points against the code and its pins.** "Red" is the number of #37013 cases that fail when the named line is ablated at this head.

| Card point | Code | Pin |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1. the platform's registration is stamped; no other write carries the stamp | `register`, `metadata-manager.ts:1301-1303` | strip removed: 2 red. Holds at this seam only (R2) |
| 2. the platform's write fills the bare slot only | `slottedWriteKey`, `package-slotted-store.ts:822` | 4 red |
| 2. the platform's removal takes its own record only | `storePlatformRemovalKeys` `:957`, `unregisterAt` `:2431`, `DatabaseLoader.delete` `:2395-2402` | routed through `removalOf`: 2 red; row check always true: 1 red; the memory loader and the peer: 0 red (R5) |
| 3. a package's first item never takes over the platform's slot | `slottedWriteKey` `:830`, loader predicate `database-loader.ts:2090` | 7 red; predicate off: 2 red. Bundled type: R4 |
| 3. an environment write | none | R7 |
| 4. a read naming no package is unchanged; `getPlatformItem` | `readPlatformEntry` `:926`, `getPlatformItem` `:1611` | loader fallback off: 1 red; the two CONTROL cases stay green |
| a stored row keeps its stamp when the boot pass re-registers it | the exception at `:1303` | made unconditional: 0 red (R5) |
| the spec value | `metadata-protection.zod.ts:63` | value removed: 1 red, its control green |

The author's four ablations reproduce: 4, 7, 2 and 2 red here against 4, 6, 1 and 2 claimed. The two higher counts are cases added after the ablations were run.

**Per path.**

- *Register.* `storeWriteKey` and `storeRowWriteKey` share `slottedWriteKey`, so the registry and the rows pick the same slot. A stamped body naming a package is that package's item (`isPlatformOrigin`, `:891`). Correct.
- *Unregister.* Judged on the registry with nothing to refuse, and `platformOnly` is carried to every loader whatever the registry held, so a row is removed where the registry is cold. `DatabaseLoader` checks each row's stored body. Correct for the by-package types; R8 for the others.
- *Cluster peers.* `receivedRemovalOf` drops a malformed `platformOnly` as it drops a malformed `packagelessOnly`, and the peer deletes by `storePlatformRemovalKeys`. On a probe (two managers over one driver and a bus) the peer kept the package's item, its loader copy and its row. Correct, and unpinned (R5). A peer on the release before this one does not know the key and reads the removal as one by name, which is what the origin itself did before this PR: no finding.
- *A peer hearing of a write.* Unchanged: `invalidateForForeignWrite` (`:4509`) drops every registry slot of the name. That is what makes R2's and R3's loader readings reachable on a running node.
- *Rehydration.* The exception at `:1303` keeps the stamp on a body a `datasource:` loader handed out. Whether the boot pass is handed the platform's row at all is R3.
- *The protocol's write door.* `saveMetaItem` removes `_provenance` by key before it persists (`protocol-save.ts:571`, `DERIVED_PROVENANCE_KEYS`), whatever its value, and that is pinned (`protocol-derived-provenance-doors.test.ts`). A write through it cannot store the stamp. No change needed there.

**R2 (must-fix): the stamp rule holds at `register` and nowhere else.** The PR states the rule three times, in the option's doc, the changeset and the schema's comment: only a registration with `origin: 'platform'` stamps a body, and every other write is stored without the stamp. Four seams store or serve a body `register` never stripped:

- the artifact door saves the item to its `MemoryLoader` and then calls `register` (`plugin.ts:1544-1545`); `register` strips a copy, so the loader keeps the body as authored;
- `getPlatformItem` falls back to every loader's stored body (`:1611-1622`), and `list` and `get` read the loaders where the registry holds no entry of the name; a `memory:` or `file:` loader's body is served as stored;
- `registerInMemory` (`:1397`) and `save` (`:4305`) store the body as given. The PR notes `save`. It does not note `registerInMemory`, which is on the service contract and which `AppPlugin` calls with authored bodies (`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts:1415`, `:1728`);
- the exception at `:1303` is decided by which loader handed the object out, not by what the row held: a body read from a row and changed by its caller before `register` keeps what the caller set, and is written back with it.

On the probe, each of the four answered `getPlatformItem` with a body no registration with the option had written. The schema change is what admits the first: with the enum as on `main`, the door's strict parse refuses the body at `_provenance`.

Asked: one rule at every seam. The stamp is honoured only where the platform's registration wrote it. The door refuses the value with its prescription (Prime Directive 12) or stores the stripped body; `registerInMemory` and `save` strip; the exception reads the stored row's own stamp. One failing pin per seam, and the changeset's sentence then says what the code does.

**R3 (must-fix): the read and enumerate seams still apply the package-less rule to the platform's record.** The store's header says the rules live in one place and every seam that writes, reads, enumerates or removes asks them. The diff changes the write and removal seams. Three readers are unchanged, and they read the new state (a platform record in the bare slot beside one package's item) as ADR-0150 D4 reads a package-less item:

- `readIdentity` (`package-slotted-store.ts:1321`): where the store it is asked over holds no package slot, the bare slot answers, for a read naming a package too, and `get` asks the registry first and stops there (`metadata-manager.ts:1532-1533`);
- `admitLoaderSlots` (`:1929-1931`): a loader's package-less item is shadowed by any held slot of the name, and a loader's package item by a held bare slot when no package slot is held;
- `pluralEntryKeys` (`package-slotted-store.ts:607`): a package-less entry under a name one package holds takes that holder's key, so an unscoped plural read keeps one of the two.

Measured with the PR's own fixture and its `booted()` helper (`database-loader.test.ts:4202`), one step further: platform, package, platform again, then a process primed from the rows. The plural read hands on the platform's row only; `get('skill', name, PKG)` answers the platform's record while the package's row is intact; `list('skill')` returns one item. On a node whose registry entry of the name was dropped, with the door's loader ahead of the `datasource:` loader, `list` returns the package's item only; with the loaders the other way round it returns both. The PR's restart case passes because the package's row is the one saved last in its fixture.

So Acceptance line 1 ("both readable, each from its own slot") and the seat's request that `list('skill')` return both hold while the registry holds both slots, and do not hold from the stored rows.

Asked: the three readers ask the predicate the write rule asks. A platform entry keeps a key of its own in the plural read; a platform slot shadows, and is shadowed by, a platform item only; a read naming a package is not answered from the registry's platform slot while a loader holds that package's item. Pins: the third-boot case and the dropped-registry case, in both loader orders.

Read, not run: for `action`, `platformSlotsOf` (`:768`) calls a package-less registry slot the platform's when no loader stores it (#32560). A registration with the option is stored, so that reader no longer calls it the platform's. The changeset offers the option for every by-package type; either the two readings meet or the claim narrows to the types tested.

**R4 (should-fix): the row predicate reads the slot's first row.** `slottedSaveTarget` keeps one row per slot and asks `platformRow` of that row (`database-loader.ts:2090`). For a bundled type the row a package's first item takes over is the written member's (`:2104`). Probe, `email_template`: the environment's `fr-FR` member stored first, the platform's `en-US` second, then a package's first `en-US`. The package's write took the platform's row over and bound it, and a process over the same rows then read no platform record. The in-memory store keys by member and kept both. Asked: judge the row of the written member, with one pin.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds. The published enum accepts a value it refused, and nothing an author could write before is refused now. Both lines are in the PR body and the changeset, line-initial.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` holds and is the right kind: `_provenance` is on the authorable surface (`authorable-surface.base.json:308`), and the probe shows the value is one an artifact can now carry through the door's strict parse. It is not `none`, and nothing narrows or changes meaning for a value already accepted.
- `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/metadata` is what step 3 gives a kind on each package the diff moves. The fix for R1 moves `@object-ui/data-objectstack`, which the root changesets version; the changeset then names it too.
- The changeset ships as CHANGELOG text. Its sentence "No other write carries the platform stamp" is not true at this head (R2); it is made true or narrowed with the code.
- Generated artifacts: 44 reference pages, one enum cell each, and no baseline moves, which is right for an added value on an existing key. `TypeScript Type Check`, the three `Type Check ·` lanes, `Spec property liveness` and `Check Changeset` are green at the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **R1 (must-fix): CI is red at the head.** 73 check-runs: 56 success, 12 skipped, 2 in progress (`Test Core` shards 1 and 9 of 10), 3 failed: `Build Core`, `Type Check UI` and `Build & E2E UI`. All three fail on one line, `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts(1847,7)`, TS2322: the parsed envelope's `provenance` now includes `'platform'` and the hand-written union at `:656` does not. The PR body calls it a type-only drift left to the UI lane; at this head it is a build break of the PR's own tree. The fix ships in this PR: widen `:656`, or type it from the spec's `MetadataProvenance` so it cannot trail again. It is the only such mirror under `ui/` and `packages/`.
- **R6 (should-fix, the maintainer's to land).** ADR-0150 D4 says a package-less row that bears a package-held name is a customization, never a second item; the platform's row is now such a row and a second item. ADR-0010 §3.5 lists three provenance values. ADR-0150 carries each earlier exception as a dated amendment note, and Prime Directive 13 asks for one here, with the provenance of the ruling. The card names its parent as cloud ADR-0118, accepted since this review began (cloud PR #4965, merged as `e738843b`). `docs/adr/**` is Tier H, so the note is a change the maintainer lands; the seat says whether it rides with this PR or goes first.
- **R7 (the seat's).** With no package holding the name, or with two or more, an environment write that names no package fills the bare slot, which is also the platform's. It replaces the platform's record in memory and in the row, without the stamp, and the platform's next registration replaces it in turn; item 2's "only the platform's own record" has the same edge from the other side. With exactly one holder the write is that holder's customization (D4) and the platform's record stays. That is a deviation from item 3 as written ("fills its own slot and does not replace the platform record"). It is not one from the Acceptance line (the write does not carry the origin, which is pinned) nor from ADR-0150 D1 and D4, under which the environment keeps one package-less row per name. Holding item 3 as written needs a second package-less slot per name, which changes the store's unique key and ADR-0150: a decision for the maintainer, not a should-fix on this PR. The author's note states the reading. The seat either amends item 3 to the reading its own Acceptance line has, or puts the question to the maintainer; until then it is an open deviation, named here.
- Dev flags. `open_questions` is empty. Of the two `out_of_scope_findings`, the UI mirror is R1 and is in scope; objectstack#37039 is the seat's card and is not judged here. `packages/metadata-protocol` reads the same table by D4 and was not read for how it serves the platform's row beside a holder's; #37039 or its consumer states that.
- The realtime `deleted` event of a platform withdrawal names the type and name with no package (`metadata-manager.ts:2474`), as a removal by name does, and the watcher event carries no scope; only the cluster payload carries `platformOnly`. A listener that drops by name drops more than the origin did. Named for the consumer; no change asked on this PR.
- SQL push-down: nothing new. The loader's save and delete read the name's rows they already read, and the stamp is read off those rows; no id is materialised and nothing is joined in the application.
- Governed surfaces: none in the diff. Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-protection.zod.ts`: one enum serves the stored and served envelope and the key every authorable schema spreads, so adding the value there makes it a value an author's artifact can carry. The declaration says so (`added`), and it follows that every door has to decide what it does with the value; at this head the service's own `register` does, and the other seams do not (R2). Refusing the value at the authoring doors, with the prescription, would keep the contract as narrow as the intent the comment states ("set by the metadata service only") and is the direction Prime Directive 12 names. The comment at `:55-62` and the changeset state the stripping as a fact; they are true once R2 is closed.

`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` and `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`: a describe string and a comment, each consistent with the enum. Nothing to judge beyond R1, which is the served envelope's first consumer failing to compile.

The implementing files: the stamp is a positive mark, read by one predicate, and the write and removal rules ask it in one place for the registry and the rows. That is the right shape, and it is why R2 and R3 are one kind of gap: the predicate is asked at two of the store's four seams. A reader or a door that does not ask it treats the platform's record as the environment's item or as a holder's customization, which is the state the card set out to end.

- **R5 (should-fix): four changed paths have no failing pin.** Ablated at this head, every #37013 case and `metadata-manager-cluster.test.ts` stay green with: the exception at `:1303` made unconditional; the peer's registry branch removed (`:4672`); the `platformOnly` line of `receivedRemovalOf` removed (`:538`); the `platformOnly` branch of `MemoryLoader.delete` removed (`memory-loader.ts:259`). Three of them are things the seat asked for by name. Asked: one case each, the malformed payload included.
- **R8 (should-fix).** For a type outside `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES`, `storePlatformRemovalKeys` returns the name's one key whatever the item carries and the loader is asked by name, so a withdrawal with the option removes an item the platform did not register. `readPlatformEntry` checks the stamp for the same types. Asked: check the stamp for every type, or say in the option's doc and the changeset that the option is for the by-package types.
- **R9 (nit).** The file header of `metadata-protection.zod.ts` (`:21-23`) and the comment at `metadata-client.ts:655` still list three values. The `Skills-docs:` reason ("never written by an author") reads against `Metadata-protocol: added`. The PR body's count of ablated cases trails the tests.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-tai913`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbZeHNsF3RWcWpj7rGj`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c018389cb10add586b3555ad5cd7ed56e7c7b1eb`
Local-runs: probe — a scratch worktree at the head, removed afterwards: the PR's #37013 cases, the first review's thirteen probe cases, the author's nineteen ablations and forty-four of this review's, new probe cases under packages/metadata and packages/objectql, packages/spec/src/ai/skill.test.ts and the ADR gates, run to measure which changed paths a test pins and what the doors and the unchanged readers answer
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-protection.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts, docs/adr/0010-metadata-protection-model.md, docs/adr/0150-behavioural-metadata-addressed-by-package-objects-keep-the-literal-prefix.md + packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/memory-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/loader-interface.ts, ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts, packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-cluster.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/plugin-artifact-platform-stamp.test.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/skill.test.ts, .changeset/37013-platform-skill-own-slot.md
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Second review of PR #37021 (card #37013), a full L1 + L2 read of the delta `8b2d8510..c018389c` and of the PR at the head. The first review, at `8b2d8510`, was a FAIL on R1 to R3. The delta is one merge of `main` (`d1ce758129`, second parent `bfd1049f22`, 111 files, no conflict, an empty remerge-diff) and seven author commits over 14 files, +500 −42. The PR at this head is 62 files, +1073 −128: 18 hand-written and 44 regenerated reference pages. `main` has moved 22 commits past the merge, to `e1dee7aeb3`. One of its files is the PR's (`ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts`), a trial merge is clean, and none of the 22 touches `packages/metadata`, `packages/metadata-protocol`, `packages/spec/src/kernel` or the two ADRs. The PR is a draft, auto-merge is not armed, and it carries one APPROVED review (`os-zhuang`) on this head. Inputs: the delta, the card and its amendment (comment 7138483876), the PR body, AGENTS.md, ADR-0150, ADR-0010 (metadata protection model), cloud ADR-0118 as merged, and the check-runs at the head. Code read to judge the diff, not reviewed: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts`, `protocol-package-bindings.ts`, `protocol-registry-hydration.ts` and `protocol-packageless-overlay-migration.ts`, `packages/spec/src/shared/protection.zod.ts`, `packages/metadata-core/src/objects/sys-metadata.object.ts`, the callers of `registerInMemory` under `packages/`, and the files the private part of this review's report names. Line numbers are at this head.
